identity.name: RACE ECO CHAIN LIMITED
identity.industry: Circular Economy Waste-to-Value Platform with ESG-Compliant Plastic & Biomass Supply Chain

summary.oneLiner: RACE ECO CHAIN LIMITED is building India's first pan-India, ESG-compliant, digitally tracked waste aggregation and recycling platform, converting unorganized plastic and biomass waste into verified raw materials for regulated industries, leveraging mandatory EPR, biomass co-firing, and CBG blending policies to capture structural demand. The proposed demerger into three focused entities (plastic, biomass, recycled products) unlocks hidden value and aligns capital allocation with high-growth verticals.

one-line thesis: RACE ECO CHAIN LIMITED is building India's first pan-India, ESG-compliant, digitally tracked waste aggregation and recycling platform, converting unorganized plastic and biomass waste into verified raw materials for regulated industries, leveraging mandatory EPR, biomass co-firing, and CBG blending policies to capture structural demand. The proposed demerger into three focused entities (plastic, biomass, recycled products) unlocks hidden value and aligns capital allocation with high-growth verticals.
financial scorecard / credit view: ₹618.75 crore / ₹14.20 crore / ₹7.29 crore / ₹-1.25 crore (FY26 Consolidated); no credit rating
guidance / outlook: Focus on scaling digital supply chain via RACE App, expanding collection centers, achieving EPR compliance, and driving margin improvement through value-added recycling and operational efficiencies. Demerger plan approved by Board to unlock value across three business segments.
order book & pipeline: N/A (B2B supply contracts with recyclers, FMCG brands, and power plants; no public order book disclosed)
segment / subsidiary detail: PET Waste (Standalone FY26): 80,609 MT aggregated, ₹363.68 crore revenue, 2.13% EBIT margin; Biomass (Standalone FY26): 10,140 MT aggregated, ₹8.27 crore revenue, 3.22% EBIT margin; Restore (Recycled Products, Standalone FY26): ₹9.88 crore revenue, 16.83% EBIT margin; Consolidated FY26: 1,44,737 MT total waste aggregated, ₹618.75 crore revenue, 2.30% EBITDA margin, 1.18% PAT margin
growth verticals / optionality: Demerger into three listed entities (plastic waste, biomass, recycled products) to unlock standalone valuations; expansion into 4 new collection centers (Roorkee, Haridwar, Rishikesh, Dehradun); AI integration in RACE App for dynamic pricing and market intelligence; scaling recycled PET (rPET) production to meet 30-60% mandatory recycled content rules by FY2028-29; leveraging Ganesha Ecosphere partnership for end-to-end traceability and brand partnerships
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 2.30% (FY26 consolidated), up 55 bps YoY; PAT margin: 1.18% (FY26 consolidated), up 42 bps YoY. Cost pressure from 25% raw material price increase partially absorbed; margin expansion driven by scale, digital efficiency, and higher-margin recycled product sales (Restore brand at 16.83% EBIT margin)
capex / expansion: Investments in digital infrastructure (RACE App), new collection centers (4 announced), and washing/recycling plants; no explicit capex figure disclosed, but operating expenses include significant working capital and ecosystem strengthening costs
capital allocation: Prioritizing network expansion (collection centers), technology (RACE App), ESG compliance, and demerger execution. Demerger will enable targeted capital allocation to each business unit (plastic, biomass, recycled products) with independent funding and growth strategies
risks & watch-items: Input cost volatility (raw material prices up 25%); working capital intensity; execution risk in demerger timeline; regulatory delays in EPR/Biomass mandates; competition from informal sector; dependence on brand owner compliance for demand pull; technology adoption lag in supplier network
non-obvious takeaways: RACE is not just a waste aggregator—it is building India’s first blockchain-enabled, ESG-certified B2B waste supply chain, positioning itself as the only verified source of traceable rPET and biomass for FMCGs and power plants under new SEBI BRSR and EPR rules. The demerger is a strategic de-risking move to unlock value in three distinct asset classes: commodity waste, energy feedstock, and branded recycled goods.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck frames the company as "BUILDING INDIA'S SUSTAINABLE WASTE MANAGEMENT INFRASTRUCTURE" — aggregating and supplying packaging waste to recyclers "through our vast waste supply chain of 300+ suppliers network pan India with a focus on ESG Compliance".
- Stated moat is organising an informal market: "The majority of India's recycled waste is managed by the informal sector, often lacking adherence to health, safety, and governance standards", with RACE offering ESG-compliant, traceable supply as the answer.
- Strategic pillars listed as ESG Focused, Organizing the Unorganized, Digitization initiative via RACE App, End to End Traceability, Suppliers' Due Diligence, Innovation & Technology, Voluntary adoption to SEBI's BRSR, and Certifications.
- Demand hooks cited: rising EPR compliance requirements, growing demand for recycled materials, ESG-driven corporate demand from "Major Corporations, FMCG Companies... pushing recyclers for organized Supply Chain for Waste procurement", and biomass-to-energy policy support.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] The Board has proposed demerging RACE's existing business segments into three entities — Recycled Products, Biomass Briquettes and Plastic packaging waste; stated benefits are "Unfolding the value of all the three businesses" and "Shareholders will get the stocks of two other listed entities apart from RACE". A committee of the Board has been formed to plan and implement it.
- [Strategic investor] Strategic alliance with GANESHA ECOSPHERE LTD, described as "India's largest PET waste recycler", including "their strategic equity investment in RACE ECO CHAIN LTD"; RACE plans dedicated ESG-compliant collection centres for Ganesha and expects "structural improvements in our operations".
- [Regulation – plastics] India's Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026: rigid plastic packaging must contain 30% recycled content rising to 60% by FY 2028–29, and end-of-life credits are removed so companies "can no longer rely on incineration or disposal certificates to meet EPR obligations".
- [Regulation – biomass/CBG] Mandatory biomass co-firing in Thermal Power Plants of 5% from FY 2024-25 rising to 7% from FY 2025-26; CBG blending obligation in CNG/PNG stated in text as rising from 1% in 2025-26 to 4% in 2027-28 and 5% from FY29; Budget 2024 allocated Rs 150 crore for a biomass collection scheme.
- [Margin pressure] Performance review states profitability was hit "primarily due to a significant increase in raw material prices, which increased by approximately 25%", which "could not be fully passed through" as the company "maintained stable margins to ensure competitiveness and customer retention".
